sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
hindiTranslation: अपने द्वारा अपना उद्धार करे, अपना पतन न करे क्योंकि आप ही अपना मित्र है और आप ही अपना शत्रु है ॥
englishTranslation: Lift yourself by yourself; do not let yourself fall. The true self is its own friend, and the true self is its own enemy.
essence: Your own inner handling makes you rise or collapse.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Your own effort can raise you or ruin you. The same mind that helps you grow can also drag you down.
simpleInsight: You are not helpless in your own life; the way you handle yourself changes everything.
detailedMeaning: Krishna begins to show the frozen Arjuna that the greatest struggle lies within. Before victory or defeat in war, a person must learn whether the self supports or sabotages itself.
modernRelevance: A man laid off at fifty spends weeks blaming his old boss. Krishna's line hands the work back to him: get up, learn the new skills, and stop being his own enemy.
translationLiteral: उद्धरेत् (should lift up) / आत्मना (by the self) / आत्मानम् (the self) / न (not) / आत्मानम् (the self) / अवसादयेत् (should let fall) / आत्मा (the self) / एव (indeed) / हि (for) / आत्मनः (of the self) / बन्धुः (friend) / आत्मा (the self) / एव (indeed) / रिपुः (enemy) / आत्मनः (of the self)
insight: Lift yourself by yourself, Krishna says, because the self is its own friend and its own enemy.

quoteVariants.text: Lift yourself with discipline. Let yourself fall, and you become your own enemy.
Lift yourself. Do not sink yourself.
I can be my own ally—or my own undoing.
Rise by yourself. Do not fall.
